center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure.

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: All drawn SLAC features are surface buildings, halls or roads. The buried linac beam tunnel itself is not separately drawn (see geometry:slac-linac-klystron-gallery's method): no source consulted gives its depth below grade, so no underground level is asserted.

name: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park campus
notes: geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-sld and geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-dmradio are drawn over the SAME OpenStreetMap polygon (way 232494549, Building 750): the SLD detector occupied this hall 1991-1998, and the DMRadio-m3 axion search is independently sourced (src:geo-slac-dmradio-prd-2022) to occupy the same building today. This is an intentional geometry-duplicate-shape pair, not an error: two different, independently sourced entities in the same physical hall at different times.

PEP-II's ring is drawn only partially (geometry:slac-pep-ii-partial-ring): the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways found in OpenStreetMap do not close into a loop and together cover only about 2,019 m of the collider's official 2,200 m circumference (src:geo-slac-pepii-cdr-osti), so no ring-length check is asserted. A fuller trace of the ring, such as a survey drawing, would allow the check.
All SLAC geometry in this map comes from a single Overpass extract of the campus plus the sources cited above.

summary.plain: SLAC's main campus in Menlo Park, California: the 3.2-kilometre linear accelerator (drawn as its above-ground Klystron Gallery), the partially-traced PEP-II collider ring, the BaBar detector's hall, and the hall that hosted the SLD detector and now hosts the DMRadio-m3 axion search.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:slac. Geometry sourced from a single OpenStreetMap Overpass extract (the SLAC property boundary way 634083231; the Klystron Gallery building way 162058026, checked against SLAC's own '3,073.72 m' figure for that structure; the two 'PEP Ring Road' ways; the PEP Interaction Region 2 / BaBar hall and Collider Experimental Hall / SLD-DMRadio-m3 hall buildings; and nine other campus buildings drawn as context), cross-referenced against the official SLAC Area Map building-number table and the PEP-II Conceptual Design Report's circumference figure.

unlocated.backlog: The SLC Design Handbook (SLAC-R-714) or the survey paper SLAC-PUB-3542 (Oren and Ruland), which should give the arc layout and the coordinate transformations; with the linac axis (the 3066 m klystron gallery is drawn) and the collider hall as anchors, the plan-view arcs follow from the published bending radius and end points.
unlocated.reason: The Stanford Linear Collider's north and south collider arcs and final-focus system, which curve from the end of the linac around to the Collider Experimental Hall, have no OpenStreetMap trace in the campus extract (only named buildings matched; no way named for the arcs or final focus was found) and no source consulted gives their path in coordinates. The interaction point itself is drawn (geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-sld, for site:slac-slc-collider-hall-sld). The two OSM buildings named "Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lab South Arc 131" and "North Arc 120" (ways 232668812 and 232669471, 93 m and 96 m across) are SPEAR-area buildings, not the SLC arcs; no OSM element traces the arc tunnels. The SLC papers consulted (SLAC-PUB-4013, -4206, -4179) give radius of curvature (about 280 m maximum on the site, 270 to 280 m in different papers) and say the arc tunnels are "not in a plane" but publish no coordinates.
